name: Hexadecimal's Numbers
description: A virus, Megabyte, loads natural numbers from 1 to `n` into his sister Hexadecimal's memory. However, she only perceives numbers whose decimal representation consists solely of the digits '0' and '1'. The task is to count how many numbers from 1 to `n` (inclusive) were successfully loaded.

input_spec.format: A single line containing one integer `n`.

output_spec.format: A single line containing the count of the valid numbers.

notes: A number is considered valid if its standard decimal representation contains only the digits 0 and 1.
For example, 1, 10, 11, 100 are valid numbers. 2, 12, 21, 102 are not.

examples.explanation: The valid numbers between 1 and 10 are 1 and 10. The count is 2.
The valid numbers between 1 and 100 are 1, 10, 11, and 100. The count is 4.

examples.title: Minimum value n=1
examples.why_included: Tests the minimum constraint n=1. Only the number 1 is valid.

examples.title: Simple value n=2
examples.why_included: A simple case where the count is the same as n=1, ensuring numbers like 2 are correctly excluded.

examples.title: Value below first two-digit valid number
examples.why_included: Tests the range just before the second valid number (10) is introduced.

examples.title: Problem example n=10
examples.why_included: The example from the problem statement. Tests a boundary where n itself is a valid number (10).

examples.title: Boundary value, is a valid number
examples.why_included: Tests a boundary where n itself is a valid number. The count should include n (1, 10, 11).

examples.title: Boundary before three-digit valid numbers
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary right before the next set of valid numbers (starting at 100) begins.

examples.title: Boundary value, n=100
examples.why_included: Tests the first three-digit valid number, which is also a power of 10.

examples.title: Boundary value, n=101
examples.why_included: Tests another boundary where n is a valid number immediately following a power of 10.

examples.title: Boundary value, n=111
examples.why_included: Tests the case where n is a valid number composed of all ones.

examples.title: Value is a valid number n=1000
examples.why_included: Tests a round number which is also a valid number. The count includes 1, 10, 11, 100, 101, 110, 111, and 1000.

examples.title: Value just below a valid number n=999
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary right before the valid number 1000. All valid numbers up to this point have 3 or fewer digits.

examples.title: Value is all ones n=1111
examples.why_included: Tests a boundary where n is the largest valid number with 4 digits. The count should be 2^4 - 1 = 15.

examples.title: Value just below all ones n=1110
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary just before a number of all ones. The number 1111 is excluded.

examples.title: Boundary at 10000
examples.why_included: Tests a power of 10 which is a valid number, starting the 5-digit valid numbers.

examples.title: Boundary just below 10000
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary before 5-digit valid numbers begin. Count is all valid numbers with 4 or fewer digits.

examples.title: Boundary with n of all ones n=111111
examples.why_included: Tests a larger number composed of all ones. The count should be 2^6 - 1 = 63.

examples.title: Number with invalid digits n=200000
examples.why_included: Tests a number containing an invalid digit. The count should be the same as the largest valid number smaller than n (which is 111111).

examples.title: Value is an alternating valid number
examples.why_included: Tests a specific valid number that is not a power of 10 or all ones.

examples.title: Value just below alternating valid number
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary right before the valid number 1010101.

examples.title: Boundary with 8-digit all ones number
examples.why_included: Tests an 8-digit boundary case. The count is 2^8 - 1 = 255.

examples.title: Large power of 10 like valid number
examples.why_included: Tests a large valid number that marks the start of 9-digit valid numbers.

examples.title: Boundary just below a large power of 10
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary right before 9-digit valid numbers. The count should be all valid numbers with 8 or fewer digits.

examples.title: Boundary with 9-digit all ones number
examples.why_included: Tests a 9-digit boundary case. The count is 2^9 - 1 = 511.

examples.title: Just below 9-digit all ones number
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary just before the largest 9-digit valid number.

examples.title: Large number with invalid digits
examples.why_included: Tests a large number with invalid digits. The count should be all valid numbers with 9 or fewer digits, as 500M is larger than all of them.

examples.title: Another large number with invalid digits
examples.why_included: Another test for a large number with invalid digits, confirming that the count is capped by the largest valid number smaller than n.

examples.title: A specific large valid number
examples.why_included: Tests a specific valid number that is not a power of 10 or all ones to check the counting logic for an arbitrary valid boundary.

examples.title: Boundary with 9-digit all ones number
examples.why_included: Tests a 9-digit boundary case where n is the largest valid number with 9 digits. The count is 2^9 - 1 = 511.

examples.title: Just below 9-digit all ones number
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary just before the largest 9-digit valid number.

examples.title: Largest 9-digit integer
examples.why_included: Tests a large number with invalid digits. The count is capped by the largest valid number smaller than n (which is 111,111,111).

examples.title: Maximum constraint value n=10^9
examples.why_included: Tests the maximum value of n, which itself is a valid number and the only 10-digit valid number in the range.

examples.title: Palindromic large valid number
examples.why_included: Tests another specific large valid number which is also a palindrome to ensure correct counting.

examples.title: Just below palindromic valid number
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary directly preceding a large palindromic valid number.

examples.title: Just above palindromic valid number
examples.why_included: Tests the boundary immediately after a large palindromic valid number.

examples.title: Large number with invalid digit prefix
examples.why_included: Tests a number where no valid number of the same length can exist, so the count is capped by all valid numbers with fewer digits.
